judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the other Wisconsin-specific forms attached to a Wisconsin risk.
judgments.clause_name: Professional Liability Amendatory Endorsement - Wisconsin — preamble

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As soon as reasonably possible' and 'specific circumstances involving a particular person likely to result in a claim' are both elastic standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces Condition 4(a) for HPL, but HPL VI also replaces Condition 4 in different words, so two competing replacements of the same condition exist for the same coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The numbering is corrupted (item labelled '4' where item 2 is expected) and the agent-knowledge sentences are clear in substance.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its imputation of agent knowledge directly reverses the first sentence of Condition 8, and the same substance is repeated in the separate WI Amendatory 'Changes' clause with a slightly different qualifier ('prior to loss' present here, absent there).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The middle sentence is visibly garbled with a duplicated clause ('affects the company's obligation under this policy breach of a promissory warranty affects the company's obligation unless...'), which obscures the promissory-warranty rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same paragraph appears in cleaner form in the WI Amendatory Endorsement 'Declarations' clause, so the instrument contains two versions of the same statutory text, one defective.
judgments.clause_name: WI PL Amendatory 3. Declarations paragraph added

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence declaring a whole condition inapplicable; definite on its face but numbered '4' in a list whose sequence has been disturbed by OCR.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the Action Against Company condition 'does not apply', while the WI Amendatory Endorsement deletes that condition and replaces it with substituted text — the two cannot both be given effect literally.
judgments.clause_name: WI PL Amendatory 4. Action Against Company does not apply

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The four cancellation grounds are enumerated and specific, though 'substantial change in the risk' and 'substantial breaches' carry inherent evaluative vagueness.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the Cancellation–Wisconsin form's paragraph (c) grounds and notice periods (10 days there) without stating which controls, so the cancellation machinery is doubled.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sixty days' notice for termination at an annual anniversary of a longer-than-one-year policy; conditional and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates Cancellation–Wisconsin (d) and the nonrenewal provisions with the same period, and this policy is a one-year term making the branch dormant.
judgments.clause_name: WI PL Amendatory 5.b Non-obligation to renew

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence has a missing preposition ('shall terminate on the effective date any other insurance policy'), which muddies the termination trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits alongside Condition 6 (Other Insurance) and the Overlap Endorsement, and it is not obvious how automatic termination on replacement interacts with a primary/excess sharing regime.
judgments.clause_name: WI PL Amendatory 5.c Termination on replacement insurance

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional on the notice containing an offer to continue; definite though commercially unusual.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrored by the nonrenewal counterpart in 6.a; consistent.
judgments.clause_name: WI PL Amendatory 5.d Termination on intermediary contract termination

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reproduced text interleaves the nonrenewal and renewal-with-altered-terms columns so that sentences run together incoherently; as written the provision cannot be read continuously.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'need not deliver notice if' carve-outs and the 60-day requirement sit against Cancellation–Wisconsin (e), which gives an unqualified renewal right subject to 60 days' notice — a genuine tension about when notice may be omitted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same interleaving defect: the passage mixes the nonrenewal and altered-terms rules and includes fragments ('aK classification of the units of exposure'), so its operative content is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The 25%-premium-increase exception must be reconciled with Cancellation–Wisconsin (e)'s renewal-on-then-current-terms right; the two provisions address renewal terms differently.
judgments.clause_name: WI PL Amendatory 6.c Renewal With Altered Terms

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The conformity rule itself is clear, but the reproduced text splices in fragments of the Anniversary Alteration paragraph, breaking the provision's continuity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: As a conformity clause it is a general reconciliation device that would resolve, rather than create, conflicts with the Wisconsin statutes; it does, however, invite argument that it overrides the many competing cancellation provisions.
judgments.clause_name: WI PL Amendatory 5. Conformity to Statute or Rule

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insured-cancellation mechanics are definite, though 'by surrender of the policy... or any of its authorized agents by mailing' omits the connecting 'or'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the first paragraph of Condition 11 and introduces a competing company-cancellation scheme in paragraphs (a)–(e), so the instrument holds several cancellation regimes.
judgments.clause_name: Cancellation - Wisconsin — cancellation by named insured

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It requires notice of 'not less than 40 days', which is an odd figure for a new-policy provision and reads as a transcription of 10 days; on the face of the document the period is doubtful.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The period conflicts with Condition 11's thirty days and with Endorsement No. 4's sixty days, none of which is expressly given priority.
judgments.clause_name: Cancellation - Wisconsin (a) New policies in force less than 60 days

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ten days' notice for non-payment, stated definitely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Conflicts with Endorsement No. 4's blanket sixty-day notice requirement and with WI PL Amendatory 5.a's premium ground, leaving the applicable period for non-payment cancellation contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three enumerated grounds with a 'to the extent that the Company should reasonably have foreseen' qualifier; the grounds are evaluative but specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates WI PL Amendatory 5.a with a different notice period (10 days here versus that clause's silence and Endorsement No. 4's sixty days), a direct numeric tension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional on a term longer than one year; the sixty-day mechanics are clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates WI PL Amendatory 5.b; consistent in substance, and dormant on this one-year policy.
judgments.clause_name: Cancellation - Wisconsin (d) Policies with term of more than one year

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It creates a substantive renewal right 'on the terms then being applied by the Company to similar risks', an open-textured benchmark whose content is not fixed by the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts against WI PL Amendatory 5.b ('company shall not be obligated to renew') and 6.a/6.c, which contemplate nonrenewal and altered terms — a genuine clash about whether renewal is a right or a discretion.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Formulaic attachment language; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The instalments are numerically specific but the first due date is 02/04/1996 — before the 03/01/1996 inception — and the ten instalments of $14,860 plus a $49,537 deposit do not reconcile with the $198,137 total advance premium, a visible arithmetic mismatch.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against Condition 1's advance-premium-as-deposit and audit mechanism, and against the Cancellation provisions' premium-adjustment rules, without a stated reconciliation.
judgments.clause_name: Pay Plan Endorsement — pay plan and past due

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement text is clear and notably removes both the final-determination precondition and the no-joinder bar, stating simply that any person may recover to the extent of the insurance afforded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly deletes Condition 5, but the WI PL Amendatory separately says the Action Against Company condition 'does not apply' — leaving open whether this substituted text survives that disapplication.
judgments.clause_name: Amendatory Endorsement - Wisconsin — Action Against Company

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The company will be entitled to a recovery only after the insured has been fully compensated for damages' is a clear made-whole rule, though 'fully compensated' is somewhat open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It materially qualifies Condition 7's unconditional subrogation right; the two are reconcilable only by treating this as an override.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear in substance; it omits the 'prior to loss' qualifier that the WI PL Amendatory version of the same rule contains, a small but potentially significant difference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts Condition 8's first sentence and differs slightly from the WI PL Amendatory 'Changes' text, so the instrument holds two versions of an agent-knowledge rule against a no-waiver condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This version reads cleanly and states the misrepresentation and warranty rules coherently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates WI PL Amendatory item 3 (which is garbled) and qualifies Condition 12's reliance-on-representations language, so three texts address the same subject.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Until there has been a determination that coverage does not exist' does not say by whom or in what forum the determination is made, and 'or unless otherwise agreed to by the company and the Fund' leaves the insured out of a decision affecting its defence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplements the HPL duty to defend and interacts with the Patients Compensation Fund limits endorsement (009-123 WI); the obligation to defend the Fund is an addition, not a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reproduced text is severely scrambled, with definitions of 'admissions', 'cost', 'receipts', 'remuneration' and 'sales' interleaved and fragments missing, so the premium bases cannot be read as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: These bases drive Condition 1's premium computation and the CGL limits provision's 'rated on a remuneration basis' distinctions, so the corruption has knock-on effects for those provisions.
judgments.clause_name: CGL Coverage Part — premium basis definitions

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The insuring agreement and the pollution and war exclusions have been physically interleaved in the reproduced text so that the coverage grant and exclusion (f) run into one another, making the operative sentence unreadable as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The grant is limited to occurrences 'arising out of the ownership, maintenance or use of the insured premises and operations incidental thereto', which must be squared with the Broad Form extensions (worldwide, non-owned watercraft) and the schedule of many locations.
judgments.clause_name: CGL I. Coverage A and B insuring agreement

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sudden and accidental' in the qualified pollution exclusion is one of the most heavily litigated phrases in liability insurance, with sharply competing temporal and unexpectedness readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is replaced outright by the Total Pollution Exclusion endorsement, while the Pollution Liability Endorsement grants a claims-made pollution coverage with its own retroactive date — three pollution provisions whose interaction is not sequenced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reproduced text has the war exclusion fused with fragments of the insuring agreement, so the exclusion's terms and its two carve-outs cannot be read continuously.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A parallel war exclusion appears in Broad Form III(B)(4) for medical payments; the substance is consistent even though the text here is corrupted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reproduced text conflates exclusions (a), (b) and (h) into a single scrambled block, and the liquor exclusion's own structure ('but part (i) of this exclusion does not apply...') is hard to trace as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Broad Form IV expressly disapplies exclusion (h) for host liquor situations, so the exclusion must be read with that carve-out; that is an express modification.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reproduced text is a fragment fusing the mobile-equipment transportation exclusion with parts of exclusion (k), leaving the provision incoherent as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (k) items are expressly replaced by Broad Form VI(A), so the fragment overlaps a provision that has been rewritten elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The elevator carve-out and alienated-premises exclusion are run together with OCR gaps ('arising aui of the uw 7 an elevator'), leaving the elevator proviso's sense uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Except with respect to the use of elevators' recurs in Broad Form VI(A), so the elevator treatment is consistent across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The loss-of-use exclusion with a 'sudden and accidental physical injury' write-back is intricate, and the level-of-performance/'warranted or represented' test is inherently contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Broad Form VI replaces exclusions (k) and (o) but leaves (m) standing, so this exclusion continues to operate alongside a rewritten property-damage regime; no direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite own-products exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with the redefined products hazard but is not contradicted by it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concise own-work exclusion; the 'any portion thereof' language is clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is expressly replaced by Broad Form VI(A), which substitutes a narrower own-work exclusion limited to completed operations — so the printed text is superseded.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A sistership exclusion turning on withdrawal because of 'any known or suspected defect or deficiency', which is reasonably specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coherent with exclusions (n) and (o) and the products hazard definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It operates only where a classification code in the policy 'includes the symbol' x, c or u; the effect is definite but wholly contingent on schedule notation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The CGL schedule shows codes such as 80613S and 75220 without any x/c/u symbols, so the exclusion appears inoperative on this policy — a mismatch between the exclusion's mechanism and the declarations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long lettered list with a mobile-equipment operator branch and two provisos; the individual/spouse branch is inapposite to a corporate insured but the structure is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is replaced by Form 009-110 WI and further supplemented by Broad Form X and Form 009-004, so the printed text is superseded while remaining in the document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The aggregate structure with subparagraphs (1)–(3) and separate application 'with respect to each project away from premises' is intricate but internally signposted; OCR gaps obscure some words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is amended by GL 99 17, which substitutes a single combined bodily-injury-and-property-damage limit and an annual aggregate reset, so the printed per-coverage scheme is displaced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence keyed to the defined policy territory; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Broad Form IX expands the territory for CGL coverages, so this provision must be read subject to that extension.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The schedule blanks are unfilled — the Personal Injury aggregate is left blank with a default rule, the Premises Medical Payments and Fire Legal per-person and per-occurrence spaces are empty, and the advance premium reads '$s Ye OF THE TOTAL' — so the limits must be derived by default.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The default that the PI/AI aggregate 'shall be the per occurrence bodily injury liability limit' must be read against GL 99 17's single combined limit, which no longer separates bodily injury per-occurrence from property damage — leaving the PI aggregate uncertain.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL Endorsement — Schedule limits

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reproduced text interleaves the architect/engineer exclusions with paragraphs (C) and (D) so that the provision cannot be read continuously as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its exclusion (5) is expressly amended by GL 99 19 (the 50-foot railroad amendment), which is a targeted modification of this text.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL I.(B) exclusions continued (3)-(5)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It disapplies exclusions by bare letter — '(b), (c)(2), (d) and (e)' as printed '{0}, (c}(2), (a) and {e}' — and the OCR corruption of the letters makes it impossible to know which exclusions are switched off.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because the CGL exclusion letters themselves are scrambled in the attached coverage part, the cross-reference cannot be matched reliably to its targets.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL I.(C) Exclusions not applicable

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The arbitration condition itself is short and clear, but as printed it is fused with fragments of the indemnitee exclusion, obscuring where the condition begins.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with the HPL definition of 'suit' as including arbitration, which is consistent in giving the company control of arbitration.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL I.(D) Arbitration condition

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant is standard and definite in structure, keyed to defined 'personal injury' and 'advertising injury' arising out of the conduct of the named insured's business.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its limit depends on the Schedule's blank aggregate and the default rule, and Endorsement No. 3 purports to add 'Humiliation' to a mis-cited item of the definitions — both create reconciliation work.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL II.(A) Personal Injury and Advertising Injury Coverage

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list is misnumbered, with two items labelled '(3)', so one exclusion is unnumbered and cross-references to it would fail.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent in substance with the personal injury definition it qualifies; no contrary provision found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The single aggregate structure is clear in principle, but it refers to 'the [limit] of liability stated in this endorsement as "aggregate"' and that space is blank in the Schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The blank must be filled by the Schedule's default rule (per-occurrence bodily injury limit), which GL 99 17 has since restructured into a combined single limit — a genuine reconciliation problem.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL II.(C) Limits of Liability

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of offences with 'unfair competition' among them, a notoriously broad and contested category, and coverage keyed to 'the course of the named insured's advertising activities'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the definition Endorsement No. 3 tries to amend by adding 'Humiliation' to item (D)1, which in the attached text is a personal injury item rather than an advertising injury one.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL II.(D) Additional Definition — Advertising Injury

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The offences are enumerated and specific, with a carve-out for advertising-related publications; 'other invasion of the right of private occupancy' is a general tail after two specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 3 amends item (D)1 to include 'Humiliation', and item 1 here is the false arrest/detention/malicious prosecution offence — an awkward fit that leaves the amendment's target unclear.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL II.(D) Additional Definition — Personal Injury

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reproduced text is defective at the key point ('mae such bodily injury afises out of (a) a condilion in the insured er {b) ons with respec to which'), so the two coverage triggers are unreadable as printed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 8 deletes an 'Exclusion (D) of Section II - Premises Medical Payments Coverage', mis-citing the section, so the exclusions applicable to this grant are uncertain.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL III. Premises Medical Payments Coverage — grant

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated auto/mobile equipment/watercraft exclusion; the OCR has jumbled the sub-lettering in item (2) but the classes are recognisable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Broad Form VIII disapplies watercraft exclusion (e) of the CGL but says nothing express about this medical-payments watercraft exclusion, leaving a small asymmetry.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL III.(A) Exclusions — bodily injury

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The liquor sub-exclusion has a confusing internal proviso ('but only part (a) of this exclusion (B)(3) applies when the named insured is such an owner or lessor'), and the war item is numbered '{45'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Broad Form IV's host liquor coverage disapplies CGL exclusion (h) but not this medical-payments liquor exclusion, an asymmetry that leaves the two provisions in tension for the same event.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Item (5) excludes anyone 'practicing, instructing or participating in any physical training, sport, athletic activity or contest whether on a formal or informal basis' — a very broad and vague class for a hospital — and the list of excluded persons is long.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is the exclusion group from which Endorsement No. 8 purports to delete 'Exclusion (D)', but (D) is the separate services exclusion, so the deletion's target and the surviving exclusions are unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: no medical expense for services by the named insured, its employees or contracted providers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: This is almost certainly the 'Exclusion (D)' that Endorsement No. 8 deletes as null and void, yet Endorsement No. 8 cites it as being in Section II rather than Section III — so whether this exclusion survives is a live question for a hospital insured.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL III.(D) Exclusion — services by named insured

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The per-person limit is stated as $1,000 with a default and the aggregation to 'each occurrence' is clear in principle, though the printed text is damaged and the multiple-coverage sentence is run into the following page.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'the limit of bodily injury liability stated in the Policy as applicable to each occurrence', a figure GL 99 17 has replaced with a combined single limit, so the ceiling must be derived indirectly.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL III. Limits of Liability (Premises Medical Payments)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All premises owned by or rented to the named insured with respect to which the named insured is afforded coverage' plus 'ways immediately adjoining on land' is reasonably definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It ties to the CGL schedule of many listed locations, which is amended by Endorsements 11, 12, 15/16 and 17, so the set of insured premises shifts through the year.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL Additional Definitions — insured premises

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of covered service categories with 'necessary' as the qualifier; conventional and reasonably bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the medical payments grant and its exclusions.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL Additional Definitions — medical expense

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As soon as practicable' and 'as often as the company may reasonably require' are elastic, but the proof-of-claim mechanics are otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Condition 4 and the HPL cooperation clause; nothing contrary found.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL Additional Condition — Medical Reports; Proof and Payment of Claim

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on 'functions incidental to the named insured's business' and on the insured not being 'engaged in the business of' liquor — both familiar but fact-sensitive boundaries.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disapplies CGL exclusion (h) but leaves the parallel medical-payments liquor exclusion in III(B)(3) intact, an asymmetry within the same endorsement.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL IV. Host Liquor Law Liability Coverage

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sweeping in effect — it deletes all policy exclusions save the nuclear one for fire damage to rented structures — and 'portions thereof rented to or leased to' is clear enough; the breadth itself invites argument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because it deletes 'all of the exclusions of the policy' for this coverage, it collides with the Total Pollution Exclusion and the employee exclusion in GL 00 32, which are stated as policy-wide replacements.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL V. Fire Legal Liability Coverage — Real Property (A)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single stated figure with a default and a Schedule override; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Schedule's Fire Legal space is blank, so the $50,000 default governs; consistent.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL V.(B) Fire Legal Liability limit

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such as, but not limited to, Fire, Extended Coverage, Builder's Risk' is an illustrative list following a general class, which is the classic ejusdem generis setting, though here the general phrase precedes the examples.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends Condition 6 (Other Insurance) expressly, and the Overlap Endorsement addresses which insurer bears the loss, so the excess structure is coherent if layered.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL V.(C) Fire Legal Liability excess insurance

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The replacement exclusions are long and, as printed, the introductory words are corrupted ('subject to the following fed Bi, fa Ae ine ee pro''), while 'that particular part of any property' is a well-known contested phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces CGL exclusions (k) and (o) whose printed letters in the attached coverage part are themselves scrambled, so matching the replacement to its target requires reconstruction.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL VI.(A) Broad Form Property Damage Liability — Exclusions (k) and (o) replaced

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Same illustrative-list structure as the Fire Legal excess clause; clear in its excess intent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Amends Condition 6 expressly and coexists with the other excess provisions and the Overlap Endorsement.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL VI.(B) Broad Form Property Damage excess insurance

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It extends 'bodily injury' to incidental medical malpractice injury but then excludes 'any insured engaged in the business or occupation of providing any of the services described' — for a hospital named insured this exception may swallow the extension entirely.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits in direct tension with HPL VII(B), which says that except as stated in the HPL part 'this policy does not apply to injury caused by any medical incident', so the CGL extension and the HPL channelling clause pull opposite ways.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL VII. Incidental Medical Malpractice Liability Coverage

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 26-foot threshold and the not-owned/not-for-charge conditions are definite; the anti-contribution sentence is broadly worded but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disapplies CGL exclusion (e) and its anti-contribution sentence qualifies Condition 6, both expressly.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL VIII. Non-Owned Watercraft Liability Coverage

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any insured permanently domiciled in' the US or Canada is reasonably specific, and the two carve-outs are enumerated; the numbering as paragraph '4' added to a three-part definition is a small mechanical oddity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expands the CGL policy territory while the HPL part and the two Wisconsin territory endorsements set a different territorial rule for professional liability, so territory differs by coverage part in ways not cross-referenced.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL IX. Limited Worldwide Liability Coverage

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any employee (other than executive officers)' with three enumerated carve-outs is clear, though the parenthetical creates a gap for officers who are covered elsewhere.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds insureds to the CGL Persons Insured provision that Form 009-110 WI has already replaced in full, so there is real doubt whether this addition attaches to the original or the substituted list.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL X. Additional Persons Insured

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It deems intentional acts to be 'occurrences' where injury 'arises solely from the use of reasonable force for the purpose of protecting persons or property' — 'reasonable force' and 'solely' are contestable, though the class is narrow.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the policy definition of 'occurrence' (neither expected nor intended), which it must override to have any effect; that override is express.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL XI. Extended Bodily Injury Coverage

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 90-day automatic coverage with an ownership/majority-interest test and a joint-venture carve-out is definite in mechanics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly contradicts Form 009-052's statement that 'no automatic coverage for entities newly acquired by any of them is extended hereby', producing a genuine clash over newly acquired organisations.
judgments.clause_name: Broad Form CGL XII. Automatic Coverage — Newly Acquired Organizations (90 Days)

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Schedule states '$4,000,006 each occurrence' against a $1,000,000 aggregate — a figure that is internally impossible (occurrence limit exceeding the aggregate) and inconsistent with the Declarations' $1,000,000 each occurrence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations show CGL bodily injury of $1,000,000 each occurrence and $1,000,000 aggregate, so the endorsement schedule as printed conflicts with the Declarations on the per-occurrence figure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The combined-single-limit rule with the financial-responsibility proviso is intricate but internally signposted, and the closing sentence preserves the total cap clearly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the CGL coverage part's separate Coverage A and B limits, and it depends on the corrupted Schedule figure in c164 for its content — the two must be read together.
judgments.clause_name: Amendment — Limits of Liability (a) each occurrence

judgments.reasoning_cat1: As printed the paragraph is interleaved with a stray fragment ('to Body Injury Liability and Property Damage Liability are amended to read as'), and the four subparagraphs plus three separate-application rules are dense.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It resets the aggregate annually 'during each annual period while this policy is in force', which must be squared with Condition 10 (Three Year Policy) and with the one-year declared term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Continuous or repeated exposure to substantially the same general condition' as a single occurrence is a standard but genuinely contested aggregation rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It repeats the CGL coverage part's identical sentence and interacts with the HPL 'one medical incident' aggregation rule; consistent in principle.
judgments.clause_name: Amendment — Limits of Liability (c) one occurrence

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition draws the familiar 'coming to rest / complete operation' line and expressly excludes mechanical-device movement other than a hand truck — a bounded but classically litigated formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines a phrase used in HPL exclusion (d), which Form 009-050 and Endorsement No. 5 amend to deem loading and unloading of patients as health care services, so the definition and the deeming provisions must be reconciled.
judgments.clause_name: Amendatory Endorsement — Additional Definition (L 9235) loading or unloading

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear as to the prejudgment interest promise and the cut-off on an offer of limits; the OCR 'Sempany' is transcription noise.
